# Tethys language and tool completeness matrix

Tethys Retrieval is a fictional mission: the solar-electric tug Argent retrieves the small near-Earth asteroid 2031 QX "Amaranth" into a lunar distant retrograde orbit after the free-flying inspector Wren has characterised it; it launches on the fictional Arcturus-5H and is operated through the fictional Meridian ground network. Every name and number here is invented. The "How Tethys exercises it" column was written against the earlier Venus-orbiter concept of the same model and is a suggestion, not a binding design. This matrix lists every SysML v2 / KerML notation form, OpenSysML tool surface, library member and known soft spot, with what exercises each today and how the Tethys model should exercise it.

**What was checked.** Open-MBEE/OpenSysML `develop` at `ac1340353c0e`, built with `make build`. Pinned OMG grammars (`./scripts/download-pilot-grammars.sh`, `build/pilot-grammars`). `go run -C tools ./cmd/grammar-coverage` was run over the full corpus (785 files: 727 productions, 483 with evidence, 0 without, 244 indistinguishable; 809 forms, 3 unseen). It was then re-run over a copy of `examples/` with `sysml-v2-training`, `pilot-corpora` and `spec-examples` removed (52 user-written files: 447 with evidence, **36 without**, 244 indistinguishable; **117 unseen forms**). The tool inventory comes from `./bin/sysml -help` and `-man`, the REPL `%help`, `api/proto/sysml.proto`, `sysml-mcp -help`, `sysml-jupyter-kernel -help`, `editors/vscode/package.json`, `internal/frontend/lsp`, `client/` and the `Makefile`. Library members were extracted from `internal/workspace/libs/stdlib/**` and grepped (word match) against the user-written examples.

**How to read "evidence".** Grammar evidence means only that the production's required keywords and symbols appear in a file (`docs/project/grammar-coverage.md`: it "does not prove our parser took that path, and it does not prove we handled it correctly"). A row with evidence still needs the proving command run on Tethys. A row marked *indistinguishable* has no literal to look for. It is reached through other productions and cannot be proved by this method.

**Priorities.** `must`: no user-written example has ever presented this form or surface to the tool, or it is core to the mission. `should`: it is exercised today but Tethys adds scale or real semantics. `could`: transitively reached, or marginal for a mission model.

**Not covered here:** systems-engineering completeness (that is a separate review).


## 1. Language matrix (`LANG-###`)

Rows are generated from `build/pilot-grammars/{KerML,KerMLExpressions,SysML}.xtext`: one row per production, then one row for every alternative form a user-written example never shows. Rows are grouped by the grammar's own section, which follows the spec clause order. "Exercised today by" names one user-written file with literal evidence, or `none` (with the corpus or test file that provides the only evidence, where there is one). The proving command is the default for the group. Behaviour rows also need the runtime command shown.

SysML v2 notes (from the grammar, not inferred): there is no history pseudostate and no `defer` keyword in the pinned `SysML.xtext`. Deferral exists only through the library encoding (see the GAP rows on deferral). Tethys must not invent notation for either.

## 2. Tool-surface matrix (`TOOL-###`)

Generated from `./bin/sysml -help` (every flag line), REPL `%help`, `api/proto/sysml.proto` (31 RPCs) and `sysml-mcp -help` (82 tools). LSP, VS Code, Jupyter, client and WebAssembly rows are added by hand from the cited files. "Exercised today by" is a word-boundary grep of user-written `examples/` (downloaded corpora excluded), falling back to `docs/`. A `must` on a flag nothing in `examples/` uses marks a surface Tethys should be the first to drive.


| ID | Surface | Exact invocation shape | Exercised today by | How Tethys exercises it | Expected output artefact | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TOOL-001 | CLI `sysml` — Write this command's manual page, in roff, to | `sysml -man` | none in `examples/`; documented in `docs/guide/01-install.md`, `docs/reference/cli.md` | Use where the Tethys CI runs need it: Write this command's manual page, in roff, to | as documented | should |

## 3. Library matrix (`LIB-###`)

One row per top-level member of every package under `internal/workspace/libs/stdlib/**` (Kernel, Systems, Domain, OpenSysML extension libraries). The exception is Quantities and Units: only mission-relevant quantities and units (mass, length, time, speed, power, energy, temperature, pressure, density, electrical, angle, information) get their own row, and each file's remainder is one row. "Used today by" is a word match (name or short name) in user-written `examples/`. **none** marks members nothing user-written uses; a downloaded-corpus or docs mention is given where one exists.

## 4. Known soft spots (`GAP-###`)

Sources: every ⚠️/❌/⛔/🚧 row of `docs/project/spec-compliance.md` (130 rows: 123 ⚠️, 5 ⛔, 2 ❌; no 🚧 rows today), every item of `docs/project/spec-pilot-gap-register.md` (29), the open limitations and further-work items of the stress-test, performance and scaling records, and the open GitHub issues (4, from `gh issue list --state open`). The constructs are legitimate mission content. Where only malformed input reaches a row, the row says so rather than proposing a synthetic probe. "Correct behaviour" follows the specification. Where the record calls the spec ambiguous, the row says so rather than picking an answer.


| ID | Soft spot (source record + row) | Smallest legitimate Tethys construct that reaches it | Correct behaviour per the specification |

## 5. Scale: what has been measured, and where Tethys should go past it

All figures come from the cited records, measured on one 8-CPU / 31 GiB machine.

| Dimension | Largest measured | Source | Tethys target | Exceeds by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Declared elements, regular one-file model, `-validate` | 2 354 827 elements (12 800 satellites, one `part def` each): 331 s, 20.3 GB peak | `docs/project/satellite-network-stress-test.md` (fleet section); `docs/internals/performance.md` | Not a target: Tethys is a realistic model, not a scaling generator | — |
| Declared elements, comfortable `-validate` band | ≤ 800 satellites (≈150 k elements), ≤ 10 s, 1.4 GB | stress test, "Where it stops being practical" | ≥ 10 000 *irregular* declared elements across 30–40 files (plan), plus a scaled variant ×20 ≈ 200 k elements | Irregular and multi-file at the comfortable boundary |
| Real (non-generated) model | a public 28-file, 7 221-line third-party model: parse 8.2 ms, `-validate` 0.27 s | `docs/internals/performance.md` (real-model section) | 30–40 files, 15–25 k lines | ×2–3.5 lines; deeper nesting and more library use |
| Load cost per element | ≈8 KiB held, ≈41 KiB allocated (4 000 elements: 260 ms) | `docs/internals/performance.md` | Report the same at 10 k / 50 k / 200 k irregular elements | ×2.5–50 the measured synthetic point, irregular |
| Editing a small file beside the model | ≤ 512 satellites (96 000 elements), ≤ 9 ms per keystroke (largest size measured) | stress test | Edit `Ops/Modes.sysml` with the full Tethys ×20 variant (≈200 k elements) open | ×2 the largest measured |
| Editing a file every other file imports | 32 satellites 0.43 s; 128 = 1.3 s; ≥ 512 = 5.3 s | stress test | `Common/Units.sysml` imported by all 40 files, at 10 k and 200 k elements | First irregular point |
| REPL / gRPC session holding the model | ≤ 500 satellites ≤ 5 s load, 250 MiB | stress test | Notebook session with all of Tethys, then the ×20 variant | Comparable, then ×2 |
| LSP over a socket, gRPC service, rendering a view or document | **not measured** | stress test, Limitations | Time every LSP request, a Python-client `ParseSources`, `-render-all` and a PDF report at full Tethys | First measurement |
| Fleet multiplicity (one definition, many occurrences) | `part sats : Block[400]` × 32 planes = 12 800 occurrences; `-instantiate` 1.97 s / 763 MB; `-satisfy` 2 412 assertions 4.59 s; `dryMass` over every occurrence 3.85 s | stress test fleet section; performance.md | 3 Meridian stations × 400 passes = `GroundPass[1200]`; 400 aerobraking passes as `AerobrakePass[400] ordered`; a 50 000-sample dispersion set | Fewer occurrences but *behavioural* (each pass runs an action), which was never measured |
| Runtime objects per unit | ≈30 objects per satellite tree under `-satisfy` | stress test | Whole-mission object of orbiter (≈7 subsystems × 20 components), probe, launcher, ground network: ≈ 1 500 objects in one `-instantiate` | Whole mission as one object, which the record does not do |
| Satisfy assertions | 2 412 (fleet) and 38 400 (per-definition) | stress test | Several hundred requirements with `satisfy`, plus verification cases | Comparable count but non-uniform expressions |
| Expression size / nesting | not quantified (“deeper expression nesting” is named as unmeasured) | stress test, Limitations | Budget roll-ups 8–10 operators deep; `select`/`collect`/`reduce` chains 3 deep; a 400-element sequence literal | First measurement |
| Inheritance depth | not quantified; inherited-member resolution 1.3× a load at 12 000 elements | `docs/internals/performance.md` Notes | Specialization chains 6–7 deep (Systems Library → Tethys generic → orbiter/probe → flight-model individual) | First measurement |
| Behaviour run length | mode machine to its initial state only (event throughput: `docs/project/archive/execution-performance-2026-09.md`) | stress test Limitations | `-advance 4000` (400 passes × 10 events); `-schedule explore:200,40` | First long run on a realistic machine |
| Calc recursion depth | sub-millisecond for deep recursive calcs; bounded by `OPENSYSML_MAX_CALC_DEPTH` | `docs/project/archive/execution-performance-2026-09.md` | Recursive pass-propagation calc 400 deep | At the configured budget |
| Scaling-design decision figures | edit-beside 512 sats 1.53 s → < 50 ms; `-validate` 1 600 split 19 s → ≈5 s at 8 cores; 10 000-spacecraft 400-file workspace from records | `docs/project/large-model-scaling-design.md` §9 | Use Tethys ×20 split into 400 files as an irregular second benchmark for §4/§5 | Realistic counterpart of the synthetic targets |

**Recommended Tethys scale ladder.** Run each step with `sysml -validate -strict -memstats`, `-satisfy -json`, `-render-all`, and timed LSP/gRPC requests:
1. base model (≈10 k declared elements, 30–40 files);
2. ×5 (more ground passes, dispersions and verification cases; ≈50 k);
3. ×20 (≈200 k, 400 files): past the comfortable editing and import-edit boundaries;
4. fleet form: `GroundPass[1200]`, `AerobrakePass[400]`, 50 000 dispersion samples, behaviour on every occurrence.

Stop at the first step where a run goes superlinear or a result differs from the step before.
